status: partial — chapters 1-9:62; the travel narrative and beyond follow in sections
note: Indexed in sections along the book's own seams: the infancy narratives and Galilean opening (1-6), the Galilean ministry (7-9:50), the travel narrative (9:51-19:27), Jerusalem (19:28-21), and the passion and resurrection (22-24). This file covers the first section. Four entries carry prior citations from the curriculum, all in chapter 6.
synoptic_note: Entries carry an optional synoptic_parallel field recording the corresponding passage in Matthew where one exists. It is a plain cross-reference: the same material appears in both Gospels, and a reader working through one may want the other. Pericope boundaries follow Luke's own arrangement. All scripture is WEB, per the standing rule in WMT G10.

entries.pericope: An orderly account, that you may know the certainty
entries.connection: The author states his method before his material — eyewitnesses consulted, the course traced accurately, the account set in order. Testimony offered with its provenance attached, which is what C08's fruit test needs in order to be applied at all.

entries.pericope: Be it to me according to your word
entries.connection: The question asked is how, not whether, and the consent is given without any assurance of how it will look to anyone. The Hidden Life accepted at the point where the cost is entirely private and the vindication is decades away.

entries.pericope: He has put down princes and exalted the lowly
entries.connection: The reversal is sung in the past tense as something already done — thrones vacated, the hungry filled, the rich sent away empty. God's own conduct described as systematically inverting status, which is the ground C16 and C27 stand on.
entries.review: PR25 removed at review. PR25 is the Didascalia's instruction about who is given a seat in an assembly; this is divine reversal on a cosmic scale. The drafter's own connection said the passage was the practice 'rather than advice about where to sit', which was an admission that the definition did not fit. Third time PR25 has attracted a status-reversal passage — after Jonah 3:6-9 and Proverbs 25:6-7.

entries.pericope: Because of the tender mercy of our God
entries.connection: The whole song turns on one phrase: the dawn visits us because of tender mercy, to shine on those sitting in darkness and guide their feet into the way of peace. C03's blueprint given as a cause rather than a command.

entries.pericope: There was no room for them in the inn
entries.connection: A census, a journey, a full inn, a feeding trough. The Sacrament of the Ordinary at the one moment where extraordinary staging would have been most expected and is conspicuously absent.

entries.pericope: Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart
entries.connection: The shepherds publicize; Mary keeps and turns over. Two responses to the same event set side by side, and the interior one is the one the narrator singles out.

entries.pericope: Anna, who didn't depart from the temple
entries.connection: Eighty-four years a widow, serving with fastings and petitions night and day, and she arrives at the right hour. The Daily Anchors shown across a whole lifetime, with the payoff arriving in a single unremarkable moment.

entries.pericope: He increased in wisdom and stature
entries.connection: Twelve years old, questioning teachers, and then subject to his parents in Nazareth for eighteen more years. Growth described as increase over time even here, which forecloses reading formation as something maturity exempts anyone from.

entries.pericope: What then must we do?
entries.connection: Three groups ask the same question and get three concrete answers: share the second coat, collect no more than appointed, be content with your wages. Repentance specified as changes to conduct already in reach, with no one told to leave their occupation.

entries.pericope: The temptation in the wilderness
entries.connection: Three approaches, each answered from what he already carried rather than from argument. Watchfulness at the gate — the proposals are refused at the moment they are made, before any of them is considered on its merits.

entries.pericope: No prophet is acceptable in his hometown
entries.connection: They marvel at his gracious words, and then try to throw him off a cliff — the turn comes when he names two foreigners who received what Israel did not. The Citizen-Stranger shown from the town's side: belonging is withdrawn the moment the boundary is questioned.

entries.pericope: Depart from me, for I am a sinful man
entries.connection: The audit is triggered by abundance rather than by rebuke — the nets fill, and what he sees is himself. Self-knowledge arriving through kindness, which is the form of it that people least expect and least resist.

entries.pericope: He withdrew himself into the desert and prayed
entries.connection: The report spreads, the multitudes gather, and the response is withdrawal. Set immediately after a healing he told the man to keep quiet about, which makes the pattern deliberate rather than incidental.

entries.pericope: They let him down through the tiles
entries.connection: Four men interrupt their day, carry a cot, climb a roof, and dismantle it. Spontaneous Service in its most literal form, and the text says he saw their faith — the friends' action is what is credited.

entries.pericope: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners
entries.connection: Levi leaves the tax office and immediately throws a feast for his former colleagues, and the objection is about the table rather than the doctrine. Merciful Reintegration performed as a meal, before any evidence of reform has been produced.

entries.pericope: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good?
entries.connection: The question is put as a choice between doing good and doing harm, with no third option available. Rule-keeping tested by what it costs the man with the withered hand, and the watchers are watching to accuse rather than to learn.

entries.pericope: He continued all night in prayer to God
entries.connection: A whole night in prayer, and then at daybreak the twelve are chosen — including the one the narrator immediately identifies as the traitor. Prayer preceding a decision, and the decision still containing that.

entries.pericope: Blessed are you who are poor; woe to you who are rich
entries.connection: Luke's version is spoken in the second person and paired with woes, so the blessing and the warning fall on people standing in front of him. Poverty and hunger stated plainly rather than qualified in spirit, which sharpens what C03 has to account for.

entries.pericope: Be merciful, even as your Father is merciful
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in the curriculum. Love, do good, bless, pray — four verbs directed at enemies, and then lending with nothing expected back, because he is kind toward the unthankful and the evil. The summit statement of Stage Seven, and the standard given is God's continued generosity to people who do not acknowledge it.
entries.review: PR22 added at review. Verse 35 grounds Unreciprocated Care exactly — giving sustained toward the ungrateful, with God's own conduct as the warrant. This is the first anchor for PR22 anywhere in the index.

entries.pericope: Don't judge; first remove the beam from your own eye
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in the curriculum. Four commands in sequence — don't judge, don't condemn, set free, give — and then the beam. Self-Accusation established as the precondition for seeing clearly enough to help, with the order stated as non-negotiable.

entries.pericope: Out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in the curriculum. The fruit test applied to speech and then traced to its source — what is stored in the heart is what comes out. C08's discernment and C20's watchfulness joined at the point where the interior becomes audible.

entries.pericope: Why do you call me Lord and don't do what I say?
entries.connection: The question is asked directly before the parable rather than left implicit in it, and the builder who succeeds is the one who dug deep. The proof test of C12 with the labour named — the foundation is invisible and is the whole difference.

entries.pericope: I am not worthy that you should come under my roof
entries.connection: The elders argue that he is worthy because he built their synagogue; he sends word that he is not. Two assessments of the same man, and the one the text commends is his own, made from outside the covenant community entirely.

entries.pericope: He had compassion on her, and gave him to his mother
entries.connection: No one asks. He sees a widow following her only son's coffin, and the narrator gives the motive before the miracle. Mercy initiated by sight rather than by request, and the child is handed back to his mother rather than kept.

entries.pericope: Are you the one, or should we look for another?
entries.connection: The man who announced him asks from prison whether he was right. Doubt in the most credentialed witness available, answered with evidence rather than reassurance and without a word of rebuke.

entries.pericope: Wisdom is justified by all her children
entries.connection: John came neither eating nor drinking and was called demon-possessed; the Son of Man came eating and drinking and was called a glutton. The generation is shown rejecting both available options, which exposes the objection as prior to the evidence.

entries.pericope: He to whom little is forgiven loves little
entries.connection: Simon's judgment is silent and interior, and it is answered with a parable about arithmetic. The woman's extravagance is then itemized against his omissions — no water, no kiss, no oil — so the accusation is turned by comparison rather than by defence.

entries.pericope: Who served them from their possessions
entries.connection: Named women funding the work out of their own means, listed as plainly as the twelve. Habitual Almsgiving recorded as infrastructure rather than as an incident — the ministry ran on it.

entries.pericope: The seed among thorns; cares, riches, and pleasures
entries.connection: Three failures and one success, and the thorn ground is the one that grows and then goes on being choked over time. Fruit produced with patience is what distinguishes the good ground, which makes duration part of the definition.

entries.pericope: Be careful therefore how you hear
entries.connection: The instruction is not what to hear but how, placed between a lamp that must not be covered and a warning that what seems possessed can be taken away. Watchfulness applied to reception itself.

entries.pericope: Who touched me? — and Jairus waits
entries.connection: He is en route to a dying child when an interruption stops him, and he stops fully — asking, waiting, letting the woman tell the whole story while the clock runs out. Spontaneous Service at its most expensive: the interruption is treated as the work, and the delay costs the girl her life before it is undone.

entries.pericope: You give them something to eat
entries.connection: The disciples propose sending the crowd away to fend for themselves and are told to feed them instead. The impossibility is not disputed; the responsibility is simply not transferred.

entries.pericope: Let him deny himself and take up his cross daily
entries.connection: The word daily is Luke's, and it changes the instruction from a single decisive act into an ordinary repeated one. Self-denial relocated from martyrdom into the calendar.

entries.pericope: It is good for us to be here — not knowing what he said
entries.connection: Peter proposes three shelters to keep the moment, and the narrator notes he did not know what he was saying. The Discipline of Unknowing shown by its absence at the exact point where the impulse is to build something permanent on an experience.

entries.pericope: How long shall I be with you and bear with you?
entries.connection: The disciples have failed, the father is desperate, and the exasperation is stated aloud before the boy is healed and handed back. Unreciprocated Care with the cost audible — the bearing is named as bearing.

entries.pericope: He who is least among you all is great
entries.connection: An argument about rank is answered by setting a child beside him and speaking about reception rather than about status. The measure offered is not who defers to whom but who is received when nothing is gained by it.

entries.pericope: Don't forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us
entries.connection: John reports having stopped someone outside the group from acting in the name, expecting approval. The boundary he enforced is dissolved rather than defended, immediately after the lesson about greatness.

entries.pericope: You don't know of what kind of spirit you are
entries.connection: A Samaritan village refuses hospitality and two disciples propose fire from heaven. The rebuke goes to them rather than to the village, and it names the disposition rather than the tactic — Non-Retaliation enforced against his own men.

entries.pericope: No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back
entries.connection: Three would-be followers, and the two who volunteer are the two who are refused — each attaching a reasonable delay. Nothing is said about the requests being wrong, only that the plough does not accommodate them.
